utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Call the case, please, Mr. Court Deputy.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Good afternoon, Your Honours. This is case number IT-01-48-T, the Prosecutor versus Sefer Halilovic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Good afternoon, Witness. Can you hear me?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I can hear you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Would you please make the solemn declaration in accordance with the paper Ms. Usher is showing to you.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I solemnly declare that I will speak the truth, the whole truth, and nothing but the truth.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Thank you very much. You may sit down, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Mr. Re, are you ready to proceed?

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: I certainly am. Thank you, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Good afternoon, Witness B. I'm going to show you a piece of paper with your name, date of birth, place of birth recorded on it. Could you please just look at this piece of paper and tell me whether those details are correct.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B
utterances.text: They are.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: May that be tendered into evidence under seal.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Any objections? I see none. So it is admitted into the evidence. And the court deputy will pronounce a number of this document.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: That will be Prosecution Exhibit P91, under seal, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: I note from yesterday Your Honours' concerns about the speed of examination-in-chief and leading witnesses through their evidence. Could the Defence counsel perhaps indicate to Your Honours the areas of contention which they would not -- in which they would object to the leading of evidence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: I'm afraid not at this stage, because we already gave some instructions yesterday to the Defence. Now you are going to ask the Defence to show their case before the cross-examination. I'm afraid that is not a practice. But anyway, you may proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: I want to lead on things which I don't think are in contention to speed things up.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes, please do so.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: I will certainly do that, Your Honour. And I assume the Defence will object. But the trouble is they may object after I've given a leading -- put a leading question.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Witness B, I'm going to ask you some questions about yourself.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: And if we could perhaps move into private session for a few moments for that particular purpose.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes. We'll go to the private session, please.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: We are in open session, Mr. Re.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: In 1993, were your parents members of any military?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Did they own any weapons?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Were there any weapons in their house?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Did they wear a military uniform?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: The village of Grabovica, was it a Croat village?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: How many families were living there in 1993?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B
utterances.text: There were 34.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: The interpreter is not sure whether he heard the answer correctly.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Could you repeat your answer, please. And while that's being done, can the usher please show P3. I'm sorry, Witness B. The interpreter didn't catch your answer to the question how many families were living there in 1993. It's recorded as they think you said 34. Was that what you said?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B
utterances.text: 40. I said 40.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Okay. Just look at the photograph on the screen. And can you identify that as the village of Grabovica?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: I take it that's an accurate depiction of how it looked in 1993?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B
utterances.text: Of the houses, yes. But the sawmill wasn't there.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: In early 1993, was the village under Croat control?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Was -- and were there HVO military police based in Grabovica?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Were they guarding the village?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B
utterances.text: They were there, but as to whether they were guarding it, I'm not sure.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: About how many of them were there there before May 1993?

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Where were the HVO military police based?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B
utterances.text: On the left bank in huts that were on the left bank.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: And in 1993 - don't tell us where you were working - were you working in Grabovica?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Was there an ABiH attack on Grabovica in May 1993 after which the ABiH took control of the village from the HVO?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Were you a member of the HVO or did you participate in the defence of the village?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Were you -- as a result of the attack, did you run into the hills, away from Grabovica, and were later arrested by ABiH personnel and questioned?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B
utterances.text: Yes, I ran away, and later ABiH members questioned me.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Were you then released and went back to your job?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Did the Bosnian or ABiH authorities permit you to continue working in your existing job?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Your Honours, I apologise for this. I should have led this evidence earlier. Could we go back into private session for just one moment?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes, we'll go to the private session, please.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: We are in open session.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: And after the takeover in May 1993 by the ABiH, how many people approximately remained in -- in Grabovica?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B
utterances.text: Quite a few of them remained. Quite a few of them.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Doing your best, about how many people? Ten? Twenty? Thirty? Forty? 100, 200, 300, whatever?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B
utterances.text: About 40.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Can you briefly tell the Trial Chamber about the age range and the gender of those who remained.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B
utterances.text: The elderly people were between 60 and 70 years old, and there was a young girl who was between 3 and 4 years old.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: How many men of military age remained in the village after May 1993?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B
utterances.text: Three or four. Three.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Were there any Croatian, Croat, or HVO military personnel in Grabovica between May 1993 and the 7th of September, 1993?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: What happened to the weaponry in the possession of the HVO in May 1993 after the ABiH took over the village in May 1993?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B
utterances.text: They took these weapons. They captured them.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: By "they," do you mean the ABiH?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B
utterances.text: Yes, that's right.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: I'm now going to ask you about refugees in the village. After the ABiH takeover, were there Muslim refugees in the village of Grabovica?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B
utterances.text: They started arriving in August. And from the 10th of May up until August, there were no refugees.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Where were they coming from and about how many approximately arrived to stay in the village?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B
utterances.text: They were coming from Stolac, Capljina, and quite a few of them stayed on in the village.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Approximately how many do you remember seeing there or how many do you know arrived to live in -- or to stay in the village?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B
utterances.text: There were quite a few of them, but I couldn't provide you with a precise number. All I can say is that there were a lot of them.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: When you say you can't provide a precise number, is it in the tens or dozens or hundreds? They're the sort of figures I'm interested in.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B
utterances.text: There were 100 or 150 of them.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Were they of mixed age and gender?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B
utterances.text: They were, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: As far as you know, were any of them armed or in uniform?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: I want to move to September 1993. You've told the Trial Chamber that there were ABiH soldiers controlling the village. What happened in the first week of September 1993 in relation to ABiH soldiers?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B
utterances.text: In the first week of September, when they arrived, then the maltreating started and civilians were killed. This was on the 7th, 8th, and 9th. On the 7th, it was calm. And then between the 8th and 9th --

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Witness B, I'll come to that in a moment. At the moment I only want to ask you about what happened before the 7th of September, in that first week of -- the first week of September. You said a moment ago, "In the first week of September, when they arrived, then the maltreating started." I want you to tell the Trial Chamber about the arrival of soldiers in Grabovica in the first week of September.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B
utterances.text: In the first week of September, ABiH commanders arrived. They visited the houses, and they tried to see where they could find accommodation when they arrived, and it was said that nothing would happen to anyone on that occasion.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: I want you to tell the Trial Chamber about the arrival of ABiH commanders and soldiers into Grabovica. I want you to tell the Trial Chamber what you saw. Firstly, how did the soldiers get to Grabovica? Or what did they arrive in?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B
utterances.text: They arrived in small buses, and there were ABiH cars that were used too. It said on the cars that they belonged to the Army of the Republic of Bosnia and Herzegovina.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Do you -- to the best of your recollection, how many buses came to Grabovica with ABiH soldiers in them?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B
utterances.text: On the 7th, there were three. On the 8th, there were three. And on the 9th, I don't know. I don't know what happened subsequently. But there were about three.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Approximately how many soldiers appeared to arrive in those buses?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B
utterances.text: About 50 or 60.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: When they arrived -- I'm going to show you photo P7, please. When they arrived, where did the buses stop?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B
utterances.text: They stopped in front of Marinko's house and Ante Maric's house.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Marinko. What is Marinko's full name?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B
utterances.text: Marinko Maric and Ante Maric.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Can you see on Exhibit P7, the photo in front of you, the place where the buses stopped?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B
utterances.text: Here, between these two poles here.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Between the two poles. I'll get you to draw on this photograph in a moment.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Could perhaps the usher assist the witness with a pen.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Now, firstly, is this a photograph of Grabovica?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B
utterances.text: It is.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: All right. Can you draw an arrow pointing down with the arrow at the bottom showing where the buses stopped.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Is it working? I can't see any movement on my screen. Can anyone else in the courtroom see movement on their screens?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: All right. You've put a mark at the -- the bottom of the -- bottom centre of the page. Can you please put a -- a large arrow going down parallel to the pole, just pointing to the position where the bus was, just to make it a little more clear.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Okay. Now, there are three houses shown in that photograph. The one on the right is without a roof. Can you identify or do you know whose houses they are or were?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Can you please tell the Trial Chamber the name -- the owners of those three houses.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B
utterances.text: The house without the roof was Nikola Kolobaric's house.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Can you just please put a "1" next to that.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Can you make it a little bit larger.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Okay. The next house across the road on the bottom left, whose house was that?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B
utterances.text: Ante Maric's house.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: And the house above that?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B
utterances.text: Marinko Maric's house.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: I apologise. Can you please put a "3" next to that.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: And you've just marked a "4" on a house above the 2 and 3. Whose house is that?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B
utterances.text: Marinko Maric's house -- or rather, Martin Maric's. Martin Maric.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Martin Maric. Okay. Now, just above that, directly above it, there's what appears to be a building -- okay. One step ahead of me. Whose house is number 5?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B
utterances.text: Ilka and Ruza Maric's house.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: And to the right of that, there's a building that appears to be behind some trees. What is that or whose house is that?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B
utterances.text: That's a cowshed.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Can you please put a "6" next to the arrow at the bottom to indicate where the bus arrived.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: May that be received into evidence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Any objections?

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: No objection, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Thank you. It's admitted into the evidence.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: That will be Prosecution Exhibit P92.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: And I believe that yesterday we also admitted some documents into the evidence concerning with the witness's markers on those photos yesterday. The number might not be correct. Maybe the court deputy could correct those numbers at this moment.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour. The two documents that we marked by the witness yesterday were originally marked as IC002 and IC003. Pursuant to the revision, those exhibit wills now be Prosecution Exhibit P89 and P90 respectively.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Thank you. You may proceed, Mr. Re.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Now, Witness B, do you know or -- or were you told why the bus stopped in that particular spot which you've marked as -- that you've marked as number 6 on Exhibit P92? Why did the bus stop there?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B
utterances.text: The bus stopped there so that the ABiH could disembark and rest in the houses and prepare for further attacks in the direction of Mostar.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Which houses are you referring to when you say "prepare to rest in the houses"?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B
utterances.text: The houses I have marked here.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: How do you know that they were going to rest in those particular houses?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B
utterances.text: Because the representatives of the ABiH had secured them previously.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Was that something you saw or something you were told?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B
utterances.text: The owners of these houses told me that.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: What did they say to you about the ABiH securing your -- securing their houses or wishing to use those houses for accommodation?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B
utterances.text: That they were going to be accommodated there and rest there, and they were assured that nobody would mistreat them or do anything to them.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Now, you mentioned some owners. Was Marinko Maric one of those people who told you that?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: When he told you that, did he indicate whether he willingly or unwillingly allowed the ABiH to use his house for accommodation?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B
utterances.text: Willingly, because he thought he would be safe. He thought he would be safe if he did that.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: And did he tell you who from the ABiH he had these discussions with?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B
utterances.text: Vehbija Karic, Sefer Halilovic, and I don't know who else.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: When did he tell you this?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B
utterances.text: In late August. It was either in August or early September. I can't be sure.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: What contact did you have, Witness B, with the ABiH soldiers when they -- after they disembarked from the buses, I think you said on the 7th of September, 1993? Firstly on that day and then I'll take you to other days.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B
utterances.text: The 7th was a good day. There were no problems.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Did you speak to the soldiers?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B
utterances.text: Just general things. Nothing special.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Were you made aware of who the soldiers were or where they were from?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B
utterances.text: They said they were from Sarajevo.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Was there anything about their accents that either confirmed that to you or suggested otherwise?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B
utterances.text: Their accents confirmed it.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Were they in uniform and were they armed?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: That's yes to both?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: What sort of uniforms were they wearing?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B
utterances.text: Camouflage.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: What about their insignia? What sort of insignia did the soldiers have?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B
utterances.text: Some had insignia saying "Army BH," and others didn't have any insignia.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Do you remember what they were armed with?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B
utterances.text: Automatic rifles.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Did they tell you, either on that day or on any of the subsequent days, which units they were from?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: I asked you a few moments back about the arrival of the buses and people's houses, that you said -- which was where they were going to be accommodated. Did you see the soldiers go into any private homes on the 7th -- on the first day they came there, which you said was the 7th of September?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B
utterances.text: No, only those houses in which they were accommodated. That's where they were.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: And for the record, those were the ones that you identified in Exhibit P92 a few moments ago.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: You said you saw them go into the houses. Doing your best, was it in the morning, afternoon, or evening, or night?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B
utterances.text: It was in the morning, at about 8.00.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: And just briefly, how were they going in? Was it in groups or individually or in what manner?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B
utterances.text: I wasn't near enough to see that, but I think they went in one by one.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: You told the Trial Chamber a little earlier that September the 7th, the first day of the arrival of these soldiers, was a good day. I want you to tell the Trial Chamber about the next day, starting in the morning. What happened in the morning of the second day, which was the 8th?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B
utterances.text: On the 8th of September, as soon as the second group arrived, shooting started, shooting, noise. They were going to houses, maltreating people, taking away livestock, and so on.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Just going back, you said "as soon as the second group arrived." When did the second group arrive? How did they arrive? And where did they arrive to or where did they -- where did -- what was their point of disembarkation in the village?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B
utterances.text: It was the same point and about the same time, 8.00 or 8.30 approximately, and it was at the same location.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Was it also in buses and cars, or was it in some other way?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B
utterances.text: Yes, yes. Just like the first group.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Did you see them arrive yourself, or was it something you were told about?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B
utterances.text: No, no. From afar, I could see but we couldn't move freely, so you couldn't see who or what.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: I just -- I just want to clarify that. Are you telling the Trial Chamber -- I withdraw that. How did you become aware that this second group of soldiers had arrived in the same point in the village as the soldiers the day before?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B
utterances.text: I saw them from my house. It was not a long way away from there.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: You said shooting started. At approximately what time did the shooting start? Can you describe to the Trial Chamber the shooting. Like, where it was from, how long it lasted, and so on.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B
utterances.text: As soon as they started leaving the buses.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: How long did the shooting go on for?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B
utterances.text: It was intermittent. They would shoot and then stop and then start again.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Until when?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B
utterances.text: The whole day. And you could hear them at night as well.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: You were at home that day?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B
utterances.text: On the 8th, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Did any soldiers come to your house on that day?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: How many soldiers came?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B
utterances.text: Three.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: When was that?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B
utterances.text: It was just before evening.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Were they ABiH soldiers?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Did you speak to them?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B
utterances.text: Yes, I did. They asked if we had anything to drink. That's all. And later on they left.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Did these soldiers have Sarajevo accents or different accents?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Yes, that's Sarajevo accents?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Did anything else happen on that day - that's the 8th of September - that you saw yourself?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: I'll move now to the 9th of September, day three, the third day, two days after the soldiers arrived in the bus. Were you at your home on the night of the 8th and 9th of September?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: What happened in -- on the morning of the 9th of September?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B
utterances.text: In the morning of the 9th, at about 9.00 two soldiers arrived and they searched the house, took what they needed. They asked for money and gold jewellery. We didn't have any. And then they left.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Were your parents at home then?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Were these ABiH soldiers?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Did they have Sarajevo accents?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Later in the day, did some more soldiers come to your house?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B
utterances.text: Yes, three soldiers arrived later.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Were these soldiers also ABiH soldiers?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Were they wearing the same or similar uniforms to the soldiers -- the two soldiers who had come earlier to the house at about 9.00?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B
utterances.text: They were in uniforms.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: And what did these soldiers do when they came to your house?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B
utterances.text: They sat and talked about what to do until the third group arrived.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: What did you hear them say, or what was the subject of their conversation?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B
utterances.text: They didn't talk to me, but they spoke to a refugee who was visiting us in front of the house.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: What was the refugee's name?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B
utterances.text: Munevera Repesa. That's how she introduced herself, and her daughter.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: When you said, "They didn't talk to me," could you hear what they were saying?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B
utterances.text: They said they would kill us all.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Were these soldiers armed?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B
utterances.text: Yes. But it wasn't they who did that. It was the third group that arrived later who did it.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: What did you do -- I withdraw that. You said you were talking to a -- I'm sorry, I withdraw that. There was a refugee, Munevera Repesa, outside your house. Did you speak to her?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B
utterances.text: Later on I showed her the path she would take.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Between seeing the soldiers outside your house and hearing them speak to her and you later showing her a path to take, did you go back inside your house?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Were your parents, to your knowledge, in the house when you were outside and the soldiers were there talking to Ms. Repesa?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: When did you show her a path to take? I want you to tell the Trial Chamber what you did after seeing her talking or listening to her talking to the soldiers in front of your house.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B
utterances.text: She was confused, and she told me to show her a path she could take to get down onto the road because she was put up in the huts on the left bank.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: And what did you do?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B
utterances.text: I showed her the way, and then I didn't go back -- or rather, I hid in the hills.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: When you say you showed her the way, do you mean that you led her away from where your house was?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B
utterances.text: Yes. Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: What did you hear as you were walking away with the refugee woman?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B
utterances.text: I heard a shot and I heard my mother scream.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: About how far had you gone from the house when you heard the shot and your mother scream?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B
utterances.text: About 150 metres.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Did you look back?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B
utterances.text: No. Because they were targeting me as well.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: You referred a little earlier to a third group of soldiers. Did you see a third group of soldiers near your house?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B
utterances.text: I saw them arriving.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Just so we get the sequence clear, when did you see a third group? Was it before or after you left with the refugee woman?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B
utterances.text: It was as I was leaving.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: How many soldiers were in this group?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B
utterances.text: About ten.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Were they armed?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Were they talking or saying things?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B
utterances.text: No. They were saying something among themselves, but I don't know what.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: You said you saw them arriving. Where did they go?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B
utterances.text: Directly to the house.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: When you say "to the house," do you mean to the yard or to the house itself?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B
utterances.text: The house itself.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Was that when you left with the refugee woman?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Why did you leave with her?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B
utterances.text: To show her the way, and I felt that something bad could happen to me because no one was left where my house was, only those who managed to run away or were saved by someone.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Do you know whether that group of ten soldiers saw you with the refugee woman?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: What -- what gives you the indication they saw you?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B
utterances.text: Because they were looking after me. They thought I might come back. I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: The transcript says "looking after me." Can you just explain what you mean by "they were looking after me"? Is -- is that correctly recorded?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B
utterances.text: They were watching me leave.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Did you ever see your parents alive again after that morning?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Were you asked to identify their bodies in a morgue the following year?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B
utterances.text: In June 1994, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Was that in Mostar?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B
utterances.text: In Mostar, yes. Bijeli Brijeg.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: What were you told, if anything, about where their bodies had been found?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B
utterances.text: Below the house. That's what they said.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Below the house? Do you mean outside the house?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B
utterances.text: Yes, our house. Outside, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Were you told how they -- what the indications were of how they'd been killed?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B
utterances.text: They were slaughtered. They were all in pieces.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: When you left your house with the refugee woman and you said you went to the hills, just briefly tell the Trial Chamber where you went to.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B
utterances.text: I went down to the road and for about half a kilometre I walked along the road and then I ran into the woods through an opening.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Now, you say that was on the 9th of September. What did you do, just very briefly, for the next three days?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B
utterances.text: I hid in the woods up there.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Were you arrested or captured a few days later?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B
utterances.text: No. I surrendered myself.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Who did you surrender to?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B
utterances.text: I set out toward Dreznica, and then I stopped by Tomic's house and they told me to stay there.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: All right. Who did you surrender to?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B
utterances.text: I surrendered to the soldiers who had been in Dreznica. They came by, and I spoke to them and they told me to stay there.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Which unit were they from?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B
utterances.text: The BH army.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Have you heard of the person called Celo?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B
utterances.text: Yes. When I was at Zuka's, when I'd been taken prisoner.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: What about a group called Cedo's Wolves? Have you heard of a group called Cedo's Wolves?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B
utterances.text: Yes, I did hear about Cedo's Wolves. They took me from the house of Stojan Tomic to Grabovica to the hydroelectric power plant on the Neretva where their base was.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: How long did you remain there?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B
utterances.text: I remained there about two hours. Two or three hours.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Where were you taken then?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B
utterances.text: Then they took me to Donja Jablanica, to Zuka's house.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: And who was Zuka?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B
utterances.text: Zuka was the commander of a unit.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: And what did they do with you at Zuka's house?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B
utterances.text: When I arrived in Zuka's house, they locked me up into a dugout where there were ten other people imprisoned.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Objection from the Defence. This is the kind of matters we discussed yesterday and which the Prosecution acknowledge as being outside of the frame of this indictment and irrelevant.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: No. But from this question, I don't know what's the aim of the Prosecution at this moment. It's very difficult for me to judge on that point. Maybe we could let the Prosecution go for a while and see whether it's relevant or not. You may proceed, Mr. Re.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: How long did you remain at -- sorry, I withdraw that question. You referred to the place you went to as Zuka's house. Was that a -- a group of houses in which soldiers were based?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B
utterances.text: Yes. There were several houses. These houses belonged to Rogic. He owned them. But we were kept in a dugout. There was no electricity. There was nothing there. And it was humid.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: How long did you remain in that dugout for?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B
utterances.text: Ten days.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: What day did you get there?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B
utterances.text: On the 12th of September, late in the day. The year was 1993.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: What else was there in this complex apart from the several private houses?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B
utterances.text: There was a cafe. There was the command there. There was a cowshed, which is where we were imprisoned later on.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Where did you go or how were you fed in those ten days that you were at Zuka's base in Jablanica?

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Your Honour, we would object again for the same reason.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Well, I believe that the Prosecution is -- has just established the whereabouts of this witness after the incident, which, you know, still we fail to see the point of your objection. You may proceed, Mr. Re.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: My question is: How were you fed or where did you go to eat in those ten days you were in the dugout at Zuka's base in Jablanica?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B
utterances.text: We went to eat in the restaurant called Prenj [phoen]. We went out to the main road to Mostar. It was about 1 kilometre to the restaurant. And that is where we had breakfast, lunch, and dinner.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: You described -- I withdraw that.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: You described a cafe and you said "the command was there." Did you pass this cafe when you went to the restaurant for your breakfast, lunch, and dinner?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: How did you know it was a command inside the cafe?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B
utterances.text: Well, that's what the others who had arrived before me told me.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: You've described it as Zuka's house or base and a unit, that he commanded a unit. What was the unit called?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B
utterances.text: It was called Zuka's army.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: And was that also -- was that an ABiH unit?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B
utterances.text: Under their control.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: I asked you earlier about a person called Celo. Did you see a person called Celo at Zuka's base when you were there in those ten days?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B
utterances.text: Yes. Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Where did you see him and who did you see him with?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B
utterances.text: Celo, Zuka, Sefer Halilovic, and I don't know who else were in front of the base.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Whereabouts did you see them? You said "in front of the base." Can you just tell us where you mean by "in front of the base."

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B
utterances.text: On the cafe terrace.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: What were they doing?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B
utterances.text: They were standing there.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Were they talking?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Could you hear what they were saying?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: How did you know who they were?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B
utterances.text: Another prisoner who was with me told me who they were.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Who was that prisoner?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B
utterances.text: Mirko Zelenika.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Did he tell you how he knew who these people were?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: What did he say to you to indicate how he knew who those three people were?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B
utterances.text: He had seen them. He had seen them on television. He'd seen them in the newspapers and in the hotel in Jablanica they had meetings there.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: They had meetings -- do you mean meetings with Mr. Zelenika or meetings amongst themselves.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B
utterances.text: Mirko Zelenika was part of the authorities in Jablanica until a certain part of time, until this changed. Then I believe that they would see each other.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: To be clear on that, are you saying Mr. Zelenika told you he had had meetings with those three people, Celo, Zuka, and Sefer Halilovic, and that was how he knew who they were?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B
utterances.text: No. No. No. He didn't have meetings.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Is your evidence that he told you he had seen these people before and that's how he knew who they were?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: And did you remain in ABiH custody until you were registered by the International Committee of the Red Cross on the 1st of March, 1994 and then were exchanged?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B
utterances.text: We were registered on the 16th of November, 1993. From the 12th of September, they had no access to us. They couldn't visit us and they didn't even know where we were.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: And following your registration on the 16th of November, were you remaining in ABiH custody until you were exchanged for prisoners on the other side on the 1st of March?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B
utterances.text: Yes. Yes. Yes, in the museum in Jablanica.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Okay. I'm going to show the witness a series of photographs in order P79, 80, 81, 82, 83, and 85. And this is for the purpose of the witness identifying locations or houses, the names of the owners of which are already recorded on the photographs themselves. You understand what I'm going to ask you to do, Witness B? That is, to look at those photographs and to tell me whether the names and numbers are correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Can we start with P79, please. It may be quicker for us to do this in Sanction. We're not asking the witness to mark on any -- any --

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: The first one is P79. Witness B, can you clearly see the markings 10 through to 16? Number 10 says "Sawmill." Number 15 says, "railway station." The next are named Croatian names.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: You can see a number of houses, a number of numbers and arrows pointing to them. Can you just tell the Court whether or not each of those markings is correct and the houses -- the numbers correctly identify the houses and the owners.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B
utterances.text: Yes. Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: If we'd move to the next one, please, which is Exhibit P80.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Can that be shown in Sanction, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Number 17 and 18, Josip Brekalo and the TV tower. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B
utterances.text: Yes. Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Please, can the next one be broadcast in Sanction, which is Exhibit P81, which will be numbers 20 through 26.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Can you see that, Witness B, numbers -- number 20 is the hydroelectric administration building. The remaining six bear Croatian names. Are those markings correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Please turn now to Exhibit P82. Again, numbers 23 through 31, number 28a is Stjepan Mandic's stable, to translate it for you. Is that likewise correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Please turn now to P83.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Numbers 30 through to 32a, the last one Ivan Saric's stable.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Are those markings correct? Do they correctly identify the location of those houses or objects?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Turn now to Exhibit P85, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Number 33, marked as Ilka and Stoja Miletic.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Meaning the markings are correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Can the photograph in ERN 04020958 please be shown.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Can you identify that as an overhead shot of Jablanica?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: May that be tendered into evidence, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Any objections?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Donja Jablanica.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: No objection, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Thank you. It's admitted into the evidence.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: That been Prosecution Exhibit P93.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Now, on this Exhibit P93, I wish you to take your pen. Now, firstly you'll see two markings. One is a "1" on the right with two arrows. What is that -- what are the arrows pointing to?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B
utterances.text: They are pointing to the location of Zuka's base. The first arrow is pointing to the location of the cafe. And these are the houses that the soldiers were in. And we were held in the area in the woods close to the cafe.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: I'll get you to mark on that in a moment.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: First are we broadcasting in Sanction or with the e-court?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: It's for the e-court at the moment. It's for the e-court on at moment.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: There's an arrow on the left which is a "2." What is that -- what is that pointing in the direction of?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B
utterances.text: It's pointing in the direction of Mostar.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Now, I want you to get the marker pen, if that's the correct technical description, and I want you to circle the two houses which number 1 is pointing to.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: You've drawn a squiggly line around the bottom of those houses. What does that indicate?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B
utterances.text: This is Rogic's house. Privately owned houses where Zuka's troops were located. And the circle was made around the cafe. That's where the command was.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: I'm sorry, you said the circle is around the cafe. I want you to indicate clearly what the cafe -- which one the cafe is. Could you draw a -- maybe an "X" to indicate where the cafe is.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Could that section possibly be enlarged on the screen? It may assist the witness in drawing his "X" on where the cafe is.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: All right. Let's start again, Witness B. Let's start again. It's -- it's been refreshed or -- or cleaned. We can see the houses much more clearly now. I want you to draw an "X" in the spot where you were -- you and the other prisoners were held.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Okay. You've drawn a circle. Is that to indicate where you were held, in that wooded area?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Okay. Now, perhaps we could use numbers. Can you put a number "1" where the cafe was. Thank you. It's been pointed out to me there's already a "1" there. Can you put an "A," another one, an "A" where the cafe was.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: And "B," "C," and "D," or "E," "F" for the houses or buildings that -- the remainder of the houses or buildings comprising Zuka's base.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Where are were you -- oh, sorry, where did you see Sefer Halilovic, Celo, and Zuka talking outside the cafe? Can you put a -- perhaps an "X"."

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B
utterances.text: In front?

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: An "X" on the spot.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: May that be tendered into evidence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Any objections?

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: No objection, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Thank you. It's admitted into the evidence.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: That been Prosecution Exhibit P94.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Can the witness please be shown firstly Exhibit P9, followed by P76, then P77.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Is that the Grabovica hydroelectricity plant?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Is that where Cedo's Wolves were that you referred to earlier?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B
utterances.text: Yes. How should I put it?

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues] ... please.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Those three houses, were they part of Zuka's base?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Is the cafe shown there?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: And finally, on this particular issue, P77. Are those two houses -- were those two houses part of Zuka's base in Donja Jablanica?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Could the witness please be shown Exhibit P86.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Do you recognize this as an overhead -- or an aerial photograph of Grabovica?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: I want you to draw with the marker pen on this exhibit. I want you to, first of all, circle -- first of all, can you see your parents' house there?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B
utterances.text: Yes. Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Should we be in private session for this particular exhibit?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes. We'll go to the private session, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: The same exercise. And I'm only doing this to show a different angle where things happened. You told the Court earlier about some refugees being housed in Grabovica. Can you see the place where they were housed on this map?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B
utterances.text: On the left. Some of them were in the huts and others in the houses, but you can't see the houses. There were the huts here.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Is the pen not working?

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Can you just mark with a "1" where the refugees were housed, a "1".

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B
utterances.text: These huts were constructed later, the two huts that you can see. It's more or less like this.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: You've drawn a "1" and a "2". Are you indicating that those were refugee huts?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B
utterances.text: No. I've made a mistake. You can't see them.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues] ... then.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B
utterances.text: You can see part of them here at the point marked with a "1."

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Okay. Now, can you mark with a "2" the place where the ABiH buses arrived, which you said was near Marinko Maric's house.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Can you mark Marinko Maric's house with a "3."

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B
utterances.text: Marinko and Ante.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Yes. The railway -- the railway with a "4."

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: The house of Andrija Dreznjak with a "5."

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: And the house of Zivko Dreznjak with a "6."

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: And the house of Marko Ramljak [phoen] with a "7."

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Thank you. May that also be tendered into evidence, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Any objections?

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: No objection, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Thank you. It's admitted into evidence.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: That will be Prosecution Exhibit P96.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: [Microphone not activated]

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Microphone, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: What time are Your Honours intending to go to on --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: What time are you going to wind up your direct examination?

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: It will take me probably about ten -- I think ten more minutes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Well, I hope you could finish your direct examination as soon as possible. We've spent a lot of time marking those photos and we don't see there are any points at this stage. Maybe later on they could be used.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Can I indicate to the Trial Chamber, this is the first witness who - and I'm setting the scene for the rest of the trial, in terms of the identification of all the places and houses in the village -

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: That's just what I thought. You may proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: May it please Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Witness B, I wish to show you a list, which is Prosecution Exhibit -- sorry, ERN 03428984. It's a list of names which -- which corresponds to the names of the people listed in paragraph 21 on the indictment. It's on two pages.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Perhaps if the witness could be shown a one-page paper list, which may facilitate his reading of it. Can this please be broadcast on Sanction.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: The first name on -- first of all, Mr. Witness B, have a look at that list. I've shown you this list before. Do you know -- do you recognize all the names of the people on this list and did you know all of these people personally?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: I'm going to ask you about each of the people on the list. Firstly, Pero Culjak. Where did Pero Culjak live in 1993?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B
utterances.text: In 1993, he lived at Copi and afterwards with his wife Matija he came to Grabovica to stay with his son-in-law Josip Brekalo and his daughter, Luca Brekalo.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Were they living in -- that is, he and his wife, Matija, who's listed number 2 on that list, were they living in Grabovica or staying in Grabovica at the beginning of September 1993?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: When was the last time you saw these two people?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B
utterances.text: In September. On the 5th or 6th of September.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Moving to the next two, numbers 3 and 4, Cvitan Lovric and Jela Lovric.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B
utterances.text: Cvitan and Jela Lovric lived at Copi, not as it says here "Grabovica" in the case of Jela. They were at Copi. Number 4 should also say Copi.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Do you know whether they were living or staying in Grabovica in September 1993?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B
utterances.text: No. They were at Copi.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: When was the last time you saw them?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B
utterances.text: The last time, in May 1993, when we had the mass.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Moving to the next two, Mara Mandic and Ivan Mandic.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Who were these people?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B
utterances.text: They were neighbours, not relatives.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Did they live in Grabovica? And if so, were they living there in September 1993?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: When was the last time you saw these --

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: When was the last time you saw firstly Mara Mandic and then Ivan Mandic?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B
utterances.text: Mara Mandic in late August and Ivan Mandic in early September.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: The next one on the list is Ilka Miletic.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B
utterances.text: In late August.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: When you said "August and September for the last answer and this one, were you referring to 1993?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B
utterances.text: Yes. Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Well, Mr. Re, I think this practice will take a long time. Maybe you could just ask some general questions to this witness, because this witness will not testify whether those people are killed or not on that day but only to prove that there are such kind of people there.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Well, it's a circumstantial -- for some of the deaths the Prosecution has to prove, we have to do so circumstantially by showing that the people were in the village or living there at the time. In the absence of a concession from the Defence, they were in fact living there. Unless we have a witness testify that they were, there'll be no evidence before the Trial Chamber --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: -- that these people even existed. That's my difficulty.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes. So just ask general questions: Do you know all those people listed there in this list, whether they lived there, you know, before, you know, September 1993 or something. You don't have to go one by one.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Witness B, you've heard His Honour Judge Liu. You told us earlier you knew each of these people personally. Were they all living in the Grabovica --

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: -- village or close locality in September 1993?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B
utterances.text: I will only read out the ones where this is incorrect and tell you where they were.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Please. And, Mr. Witness B, be aware that the top of the column is where -- the places listed is the place of birth, not the place of residence.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B
utterances.text: Pero Culjak, Grabovica; Matija Culjak, Grabovica; Cvitan Lovric, Copi; Jela Lovric, Copi.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Sorry. You said you were only going to read out the ones which were incorrect and tell you where they are. What do you mean by "incorrect"?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B
utterances.text: Jela Lovric, the location of the crime was in Copi, not in Grabovica.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: All right. I've been asked to -- instructed to ask you general questions about where the people lived and when you last saw them. Have you ever seen any of these people since the day you left the village, the 9th of September, 1993?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: And going back to my earlier question: Apart from Jela Lovric, were all the other people -- and Cvitan Lovric, were all the other people living in Grabovica as of September 1993?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B
utterances.text: Jozo Istuk, he wasn't.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Where was he living?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B
utterances.text: Near Copi, near Dreznica. It was in Dreznica.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: When did you last see him, Witness B?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B
utterances.text: I do not recall.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Numbers 15 and 16 on the list, Andrija Dreznjak and Mara Dreznjak, when did you last see those two people?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B
utterances.text: On the 9th of September, 1993.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Where were they when you last saw them?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B
utterances.text: In front of their house.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: You said there were soldiers in the village. Were there any soldiers in their vicinity when you last saw them?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B
utterances.text: In front of their house, and their daughter, Dragica Dreznjak as well.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: What were the soldiers doing?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B
utterances.text: They were talking, but I don't know what about.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: And where were Andrija and Matija -- I'm sorry, Mara Dreznjak and their daughter, Dragica, when the soldiers were talking? Were the soldiers talking to them or were the soldiers talking amongst themselves?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B
utterances.text: They were in front of their house. But whether they were talking to them, probably they were.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Were these soldiers armed?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Did you hear what happened to these people?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B
utterances.text: When there was an exchange of bodies, only Dragica Dreznjak was identified. As for Mara and Andrija Dreznjak, they are missing.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Were you told where Dragica's body was found?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: For the clarity of the record, were these soldiers you saw them with, were they ABiH soldiers?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: That completes my examination-in-chief, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Oh, I'm sorry, the tender of that particular document. Would that assist the Trial Chamber?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Well, you could do that later on, after the cross-examination. Maybe during the cross-examination the Defence will raise some questions concerning with this list, so which will effect the credibility of this list. I'm not sure. I cannot predict the outcome. So there's still an opportunity at a later stage.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Can I indicate that the list -- if we tender it, it's only as the basis of an aide-memoire to the Trial Chamber it's not on the basis of proof of death. It's only to assist the Trial Chamber by putting it in evidence and having other witnesses identify people from that list as you would from -- perhaps from paragraph 21 of the indictment. That's the only purpose we would put that into --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Well, in the Rules, there's no differentiations about the purpose of the evidence, you know. I could not understand what is the aide-memoire and what is the hard evidence in this case. But we'll discuss it at a later stage.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Well, maybe we could give it an ID number on it.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, that will be marked for identification, 97.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Now it's time to have a break, because I have been advised that the tapes is running out. And we'll resume at ten minutes to 5.00, beginning with the cross-examination by the Defence team.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes. Any cross-examination? Mr. Mettraux.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Yes, thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Would you please indicate how long you're going to take to cross-examine this witness.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Well, it is quite difficult to say at this stage, Your Honour, but I would think that we might have to go over into tomorrow morning, I'm afraid.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: To tomorrow morning? So there's no possibility for us to take the next witness today?

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: It seems very remote, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes. I hope we could finish this witness today. And you may proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: I will try my best. Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Good afternoon, Witness. My name is Guenael Mettraux and I appear as co-counsel for Mr. Halilovic. I would like to ask you if you may assist the Trial Chamber and myself in finding our way in the area where you're from, and I would like this map to be placed on the ELMO for that purpose. Thank you. Thank you. You've indicated, sir, that at the relevant time you lived in the village of Gornja Grabovica. Could you indicate with the pointer where that would be on the map.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B
utterances.text: [Indicates]. Grabovica, not Gornja Grabovica.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Could you they will place the pointer -- yes, thank you. So, sir, could you please tell us what the "G" before Grabovica stands for.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B
utterances.text: I don't know. We always referred to the village as Grabovica. I don't know about Gornja Grabovica. There is Donja Grabovica, Grabovica, and Diva Grabovica.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: We then will refer to Gornja Grabovica as Grabovica. Am I correct in understanding that Grabovica was part of a group of villages and hamlets that would be referred to as Dreznica?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B
utterances.text: Yes, it belonged to the Dreznica commune.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And if you go further south from Grabovica, where the pointer was previously, you would reach a village or a hamlet called Kremenac; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And Kremenac is a tiny hamlet, sir. There's only a few houses in that village.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B
utterances.text: Above Grabovica, yes. There was only one family living there.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And it would be about 1 kilometre away from Grabovica, wouldn't it?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B
utterances.text: A kilometre or a kilometre and a half.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Thank you. If you were to go from Grabovica to Kremenac, there was no road there, was there. There was only a narrow path, a stony or a muddy path; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B
utterances.text: Yes, it was a path made of earth and stones.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And there was no sign post in Grabovica indicating the village of Kremenac.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: So if you were to leave Grabovica, you would have to know about this village, if you wanted to get there, I suppose.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: If you continue further down or south along the Neretva River towards Mostar, you would reach another village which you have already mentioned, which is Donja Grabovica; is it correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B
utterances.text: But it's on the left side.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: That's correct. That's on the left side if you follow the M15 towards Mostar. M17, I'm sorry.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And it would be approximately 4 to 5 kilometres away from Grabovica.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B
utterances.text: Yes. 4 kilometres or maybe 3 and a half.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Very well, then. As you indicated, Donja Grabovica would be on the left bank of the Neretva, and on the other side of the Neretva river at the same level you have another village called Copi.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: It is also a very little village, with only a few houses.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: It would also be more or less 4 kilometres or so away from Grabovica, where you lived.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: There was no roads leading directly from Grabovica, where you lived, to Copi.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B
utterances.text: There was up to a place close to Copi, because there was a lake preventing further passage. But if you got onto the M17 main road to Dreznica, across from the bridge you could get straight to Copi. But from the direction of Grabovica, you couldn't reach it by car.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: That's correct. And you could reach it though on foot had you wanted to, by staying on the same side of the Neretva River.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B
utterances.text: Why would you go on foot if you can go by car?

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Well, if you don't have a car, for instance. Let's leave that for -- for a minute. It would take -- would I be correct in saying that it would take about two hours to walk from Grabovica to Copi if someone had the strange idea of walking there? Would that be correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And, again, there was no sign post in Grabovica indicating "Copi"?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Thank you. If you go further south on the map - if I can ask the technical people - yes. Thank you very much. You reach another tiny hamlet called - and I apologise for the pronunciation - Sjencine, also on the left side of the Neretva River.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B
utterances.text: Yes. Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Then, sir, I would like to take you north of Grabovica for a minute to a place called Diva Grabovica. Can you put the pointer, please, on the map to indicate where Diva Grabovica is located.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B
utterances.text: [Indicates]

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Thank you. So I would be correct in saying that Diva Grabovica is approximately 4 kilometres away -- 4 kilometres north of Grabovica, where you were living? Would I be correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B
utterances.text: One could say so.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And Diva Grabovica was famous or, I should say, was known because it had a famous hunting lodge there; is it correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B
utterances.text: Yes, a hunting lodge.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And that hunting lodge, sir, had been heavily damaged in the course of the fightings between the ABiH and the HVO.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B
utterances.text: I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: From Diva Grabovica, sir, would you be able to see the front line?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B
utterances.text: I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: But you know that no one lived there at the time.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Objection. The --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Very unspecific. The front line when and where? And no one lived there at what time? I mean, the Prosecution is at a loss at the moment to see where this is going, but my learned friend is going to ask questions generally, he should cement them to some sort of time frame.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Well, I believe that the situation is very clear, that is, the troops surrounding the -- Sarajevo and -- and the troops in Mostar. Maybe you could indicate which, you know, front line do you mean.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Very well.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Would you be able to see the Vrdi front line from Diva Grabovica? From the hunting lodge, for instance?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B
utterances.text: How could I have seen it, since I had been imprisoned?

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Would you know, sir, whether anyone lived in Grabovica, Diva Grabovica, I should say, at the end of August or beginning of September? 1993.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: The answer is yes, people were living there?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B
utterances.text: Yes, and they still live there to this very day.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Thank you. I would like to move on to another issue now which --

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: You can remove the map from the ELMO now. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: I would like now to move back to another issue which was touched very briefly earlier today; namely, the retaking of Grabovica by ABiH forces. As a man of limited - thank you - military experience, were you able to identify any of the units which took part in that operation, from the ABiH side, that is?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B
utterances.text: I don't quite understand the question.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Well, my question is: Do you know the names of any of the units which took part in the operation when the village of Grabovica was retaken by the ABiH? The names of some of those units.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B
utterances.text: I saw the flag of the ABiH and another flag with a crescent and stars.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: So you don't know the name? That's the answer? You don't know the name of any of those units?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B
utterances.text: Well, there was the flag of the army and of BH.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Very well. Earlier today you told the Prosecution that during the relevant period of time you had not been an HVO soldier; am I correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: I would like to read out to you your statement of the 3rd of December, 1995 to the Office of the Prosecutor.
